summary.text: A 52-year-old woman attended an outpatient clinic with dizziness, impaired hearing and a history of fluid accumulation in the external ear canal for several years. She denied smoking, acknowledged a history of alcohol consumption, had no history of systemic disease and had self-treated with ear drops and intermittent erythromycin ointment. Examination showed bilateral tympanic membrane invagination, poor motility and no fluid level, and CT showed opacification of the right middle ear and mastoid. The primary care physician diagnosed chronic purulent (suppurative) otitis media.

An ear swab culture grew two species. MALDI-TOF MS identified the sparsely growing one as Alcaligenes faecalis subsp. faecalis, while the dominant Gram-negative strain could not be identified by MALDI-TOF MS or Vitek 2. Whole genome sequencing identified it as Kerstersia gyiorum. E-test MICs were reported as susceptible for the 17 agents tabulated; the abstract reports chloramphenicol resistance whereas the Discussion states susceptibility to all antibiotics.

Before the culture was started, the physician administered ofloxacin and dexamethasone ear drops with 2 g/day of intramuscular ceftriaxone for ten days. Ear discharge ceased after treatment, she was told to continue the ofloxacin-dexamethasone drops, and at a subsequent follow-up she reported significantly improved ear symptoms. The authors state that antimicrobial therapy led to remission, call ofloxacin with ceftriaxone effective, and say prolonged lack of appropriate treatment delayed progression.
